title: A succession of leaders and dissension in the Blue Rhythm Band
summary: Leaders ran from Carroll Dickerson to Baron Lee and Lucky Millinder, and several members wanted to lead, causing jealousy.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Now, you mentioned everybody wanted to be a leader in that band, and they had many different people fronting the band.

Yeah, they had a lot of different leaders in front of the band. They started off with Carroll Dickerson from Chicago. He was the first leader, I think, in front of the band. Then they come up with another fellow named Sonny something-or-other, but he didn't last either... Q: Sonny Adams? You mentioned Sonny Adams. Was that the name?

No. Sonny Adams was a tenor player. But this leader's name was Sonny something. Well, anyway, then they had Baron Lee; he was the third leader that I know of. And after that, I don't know, because I was out of the band this time -- I was gone again. Then I think Lucky Millinder was about the last one that was in front of the band. It was still the Blue Rhythm Band when Lucky Millinder taken it over.
Now, you mentioned that everybody wanted to be a leader.
Yeah. There was a lot of dissension in the band between different ones. I'd rather not call their names, but it was about three or four of them that really

wanted to be the leader. And everything that happened, Downtown knew about it before it even happened. And it didn't not make for a good band, because there was too much dissension. Always something, this-that-and-the-other, a lot of jealousy and so forth and so on.
